info.title: OBI ENERGY TRACKER Public API
info.description:
Access tokens are issued by the Keycloak realm `https://auth.obi.com/auth/realms/energy-tracker-clients`
using the public client `home-assistant-user` (authorization code flow, PKCE S256 required, no client secret).
Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

## Obtaining an access token

Login is passwordless: you enter your email address and Keycloak sends a six character
one-time code to that address. The code is valid for five minutes.

The following script performs the full flow and prints the access token to stdout.
Save it as `jwt.sh`, then run `TOKEN=$(./jwt.sh)`.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
B=https://auth.obi.com/auth/realms/energy-tracker-clients/protocol/openid-connect
C=home-assistant-user
U=http://localhost/callback
J=$(mktemp) P1=$(mktemp) P2=$(mktemp) P3=$(mktemp) H3=$(mktemp)
V=$(head -c32 /dev/urandom|base64|tr +/ -_|tr -d '=')
A(){ grep -o 'action="[^"]*"' "$1"|head -1|cut -d'"' -f2|sed 's/&/\&/g';}
FB(){ grep -o 'kc-feedback-text[^>]*>[^<]*' "$1"|sed 's/.*>//'|head -1;}
printf 'Mail: ';read M
S=$(curl -sc $J -b $J -o $P1 -w %{http_code} "$B/auth?client_id=$C&response_type=code&scope=openid&redirect_uri=$U&code_challenge=$(printf %s "$V"|openssl dgst -sha256 -binary|base64|tr +/ -_|tr -d '=')&code_challenge_method=S256")
echo "[1] authorize     : $S" >&2
S=$(curl -sc $J -b $J -o $P2 -w %{http_code} -d "username=$M" "$(A $P1)")
echo "[2] username POST : $S | fields: $(grep -o 'name="[^"]*"' $P2|cut -d'"' -f2|tr '\n' ' ')| msg: $(FB $P2)" >&2
printf 'OTP: ';read O
S=$(curl -sc $J -b $J -o $P3 -D $H3 -w %{http_code} -d "code=$O" "$(A $P2)")
L=$(grep -i '^location:' $H3|tr -d '\r'|cut -d' ' -f2)
echo "[3] otp POST      : $S | location: ${L:-<keine>} | msg: $(FB $P3)" >&2
while [ -n "$L" ] && [ "${L#$U}" = "$L" ];do
  L=$(curl -sc $J -b $J -o /dev/null -D- "$L"|grep -i '^location:'|tr -d '\r'|cut -d' ' -f2)
  echo "[>] redirect      : ${L:-<keine>}" >&2
done
[ -z "$L" ] && { echo "ABBRUCH: kein Redirect zur Callback-URL erreicht" >&2; exit 1; }
K=$(echo "$L"|sed 's/.*[?&]code=//;s/&.*//')
echo "[4] auth code     : ${K:0:12}... (len ${#K})" >&2
R=$(curl -s -d grant_type=authorization_code -d client_id=$C -d redirect_uri=$U -d code_verifier=$V -d "code=$K" "$B/token")
echo "$R"|grep -q access_token && echo "$R"|sed 's/.*"access_token":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/' || { echo "TOKEN-FEHLER:" >&2; echo "$R" >&2; exit 1;}
```

## Example requests

```bash
TOKEN=$(./jwt.sh)

curl -s https://api.obi.com/energytracker/api/users/me \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.obi.companion.energy-tracking.user.v2+json"

curl -s "https://api.obi.com/energytracker/api/historical-data/<bridgeId>/measures?from=week&to=now&measures=energy" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.obi.companion.energy-tracking.historical-record.v2+json"
```

The `bridgeId` and the device ids are returned by `GET /users/me` in the `bridge` object.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: Profile of the account the access token was issued for.

tags.name: Historical Data
tags.description: Historical energy readings of the paired devices.

get.description: Retrieve the user currently authenticated by JWT
get.summary: Get User by accountId in JWT

get.description: Returns energy, negative_energy, rssi, battery_level, outlet_state for N devices paired to given bridge

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: the 'from' parameter could either be a string which can be parsed to a valid js-date or one of the keys 'now', 'hour', 'today', 'week', 'month', 'year', 'start'. Defaults to 'today'

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: the 'to' parameter could either be a string which can be parsed to a valid js-date or one of the keys 'now', 'hour', 'today', 'week', 'month', 'year', 'start'. Defaults to 'now'

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Accepts valid ISO8601 Duration strings in the forms of start/stop, start/duration, duration/stop and duration only. If only duration is supplied, duration is subtracted from the value of the 'to' query parameter (default 'now'), else duration overwrites 'from' and 'to' parameters.

parameters.name: deviceIds
parameters.description: which deviceIds (sensors/outlets) to query data for. Defaults to all bridge paired devices if not given

label.description: if label is not overwritten by user, it contains the bridges btChallengeId, it should only be used for display purposes.

displayName.description: User set-able name of the bridge for display purposes. Replaces label field

btChallengeId.description: Immutable bluetooth challenge ID of bridge. Used for identification of bridge in bluetooth connected scenarios

uploadInterval.description: Rate at which sensor sends data. Change to toggle sensor "live-mode". Acceptable values are 300 (default) and 2 (live)

claimedAt.description: Date of when sensor was associated whith current bridge/user

dataVisibleSince.description: Date of when sensor was associated whith current bridge/user

displayName.description: User set-able name of the sensor for display purposes. Replaces label field

hasSeenAdvertisingConsentBanner.description: Whether the user has seen the advertising consent banner.

advertisingConsentBannerViewDate.description: Server-set timestamp marking when the user first acknowledged the advertising consent banner. Read-only.

bearerAuth.description: Access token issued by the Keycloak realm `https://auth.obi.com/auth/realms/energy-tracker-clients`. Obtain it with the public client id `home-assistant-user` via the authorization code flow (`https://auth.obi.com/auth/realms/energy-tracker-clients/protocol/openid-connect/auth` and `/protocol/openid-connect/token`, PKCE S256 required, no client secret). Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.
